- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.7) but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–2% to offset sentiment-driven overconfidence.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when price deviates >+5% from 18d moving average; adjust forecast toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), model tends to overfit recent trends; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 periods’ values.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is consistently higher than forecast (e.g., >+2% across 5+ days), model underestimates long-term demand; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3 periods if sentiment remains positive.
